# Change Auth
- `core/auth.py`: hashing/JWT only (argon2 + pyjwt live nowhere else); repository/migration: users.
- `services/auth/`: credential/session policy (`policy.py`), bounded off-loop Argon2 admission (`_argon2.py`), and the login rate limit (`_ratelimit.py`).
- `api/v1/auth.py` and `api/deps.py`: cookie transport and authorization. Only `login` / `logout` / `me` exist; [`get_current_user`](mex://function:355a11f909bcfba98761d6d0a28493aa) is mounted once per protected router in `api/v1/__init__.py`, not per route.
- `api/_origin_middleware.py`: `OriginProtectionMiddleware` is why a scripted write breaks. The cookie is the only credential, so `curl -b tb_session=... -X POST` answers 403 `untrusted_origin` until it also sends `-H 'Origin: <origin the request is addressed to>'`. Fail-closed on a missing Origin is deliberate — no bearer path exists to tell a script from CSRF.
- Frontend: login and protected-route behavior.

Update schemas/config → core/repository → service tests → API/dependency tests → frontend/client → gates.

Verify: JWT library stays in `core/auth.py`; cookie flags/TTL are config-driven; no public signup; invalid sessions return the shared 401 envelope; empty `AUTH__SECRET` disables token issuance (login answers 503). Unsafe cookie writes require an exact trusted Origin. Sessions are stateless — revocation is a per-user token-version bump ([`revoke_sessions`](mex://function:83a95bdbe073ff6fc6f2a12adae32b2c)); long-lived streams and large-body admission revalidate that version too.
